headline: Gunmen fired on a church funeral in Jordan. Seven dead.
summary: Three men with pistols and a rifle went into a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, during a funeral on Friday and opened fire. Seven people died and 34 were hurt, AP reports; the BBC counts six dead and 28 hurt. The gunmen fled. No one has claimed the attack, and King Abdullah II called it a terrorist act.

cover_question.q: Did they catch the bad guys?

cover_answer: Not yet. Jordan's police are looking for them.
table_question: Can you comfort someone before you know why it happened?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: In a country called Jordan, very far away, farther than any trip we have taken, some men with guns hurt people inside a church. Everyone there was saying goodbye to someone who had died. The police are looking for the men, and the king of Jordan said they will be punished. You are safe here, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Far away, police looking, the king promised. Only if they hear it.
5-7.why_long: A child this age reads your face before your words and takes one vivid feature, here guns in a church, for the whole event, so this stays in the drawer unless it reaches them. If it does, the script gives them distance and a search under way. Expect "could that happen here?" Rare even in Jordan, the BBC says.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Karak, 110 miles south of Jordan's capital, has a large Christian community. On Friday three gunmen went into a church during a funeral, fired for minutes and ran. Nobody has said who or why. The prime minister pulled every minister into one room, like an all-staff meeting after a bad day.
8-12.why: Place, attack, no motive yet, a meeting called. Rare is the word.
8-12.why_long: At this age a child wants the chain: who did it and why. Here it stops at nobody knows yet, and the script says so instead of filling the gap, because children this age are testing whether adults tell the truth when the answer is missing. Expect "why would anyone do that?" Nobody has said.

13-17.script: Why would gunmen pick a funeral in a Christian town? Three men shot up a church in Karak, Jordan; seven died and no one has claimed it. Second: Egypt, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon and Al-Azhar's grand imam condemned it within hours. What does a fast reaction do, and what doesn't it?
13-17.why: A target chosen for who was in it, and a region speaking fast.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can reason about what is not in front of them: a target picked for who prays there, and a region's leaders condemning it within hours. The script asks them to hold both and say what the response changes, and what it does not. Expect "will this start something bigger?" No one knows who did it yet.

5-7.q: Did they catch the bad guys?
5-7.a: Not yet. Jordan's police are looking for them.

8-12.q: Why did they shoot people at a funeral?
8-12.a: Nobody knows yet. No one has been named or claimed it.
Rare, the BBC says. Karak's last attack was in 2016.

13-17.q: Was it because they were Christians?
13-17.a: No one has said. Karak has a large Christian community.
Early counts do. AP had seven dead and 34 hurt; the BBC six and 28.
